Replies to letter of December 4, 1974, Martin Convisser (DOT) to NSF
Paragraph 1 - Some knowledge of the geophysical conditions is now available, as a result of a long refraction study that was made in the 1974-1975 field season. (See reply to EPA letter for further information).
Paragraphs 2 & 3 - Based on the few data available on ocean currents in the Ross Sea, and no data under the Ross Ice Shelf, a slow-flowing current can be postulated under the ice shelf. This current would help to disperse any oil released by a blowout. The studies by Wolfe and Hoult were of oil under sea ice, a much more porous and permeable ice than would be found under the Ross Ice Shelf.
Paragraph 4 - No one can argue with the statements given.
